PullRequest.Title: Use Dark 2026 for component fixtures
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- bundle the built-in Dark 2026 theme for component fixtures
- switch the default Dark fixture variant from Dark Modern to Dark 2026
- keep Light and high-contrast fixture themes unchanged

This is intentionally separate from the TextMate highlighting and diff/multi-diff work. Dark fixture screenshots are expected to change; layout and behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm exec eslint -- src\vs\workbench\test\browser\componentFixtures\fixtureUtils.ts`
- editor diagnostics
- `git diff --check`

Scenarios.Scenario: CI component-fixture screenshot rendering for the default Dark variant
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing component-explorer render subprocess loads the fixture bundle, then setupTheme must complete ColorThemeData.ensureLoaded before fixture rendering and screenshot capture can proceed. The changed Dark theme adds parsing and merging of 2026-dark.json before that render; this work is on the first Dark render's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the component-explorer renderer that captures all fixture screenshots
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing render command per workflow job; fixture scheduling is managed inside that command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same component-explorer render subprocess ran before the theme switch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The subprocess must finish before screenshot manifests and CI checks proceed, but its invocation and cardinality are unchanged by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse bundled JSONC theme texts and merge colors/token rules through the include chain
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for each of four Dark theme documents on the first Dark setup per browser document after the diff, versus three before; subsequent fixtures reuse the cached promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Dark Modern was the root and loaded itself, Dark+, and Dark VS. The new root adds one bounded in-memory 2026-dark.json parse before applying its overrides.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first Dark fixture waits for parsing; later Dark fixtures do not repeat it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Theme document size and include depth, not the number of fixture definitions. The effective load cardinality is one per ColorThemeData object per browser document because themeLoadedPromises coalesces concurrent and repeated Dark fixture setup calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Multiple fixture renders may invoke setupTheme concurrently, but all Dark calls share one cached Promise in themeLoadedPromises. Theme includes are traversed serially by _loadColorTheme; fixture rendering concurrency does not multiply theme parsing within a document.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold document: Dark 2026, Dark Modern, Dark+, and Dark VS are read from the bundled in-memory theme map and parsed once. Warm/repeated Dark fixtures reuse the WeakMap promise and loaded ColorThemeData. Before the diff, Dark Modern, Dark+, and Dark VS were parsed once; the diff adds only the bounded Dark 2026 layer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added import, root theme path, recursive include chain, and WeakMap coalescing are directly visible in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact bundle bytes and milliseconds depend on the bundler and component-explorer page reuse, but the added source is a fixed theme document and cannot scale with fixture count inside a document.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The PR intentionally selects a richer theme and adds one fixed in-memory parse/merge on the first Dark render. It does not create per-fixture repeated work or new filesystem/network fan-out, and the cache coalesces parallel callers.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive component explorer startup and rendering of Dark or Light fixtures
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The fixtureUtils module eagerly bundles theme source strings at page startup. Selecting/rendering a Dark fixture then awaits the shared Dark theme load; Light rendering does not parse Dark 2026, although the extra bounded source string is present in the bundle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Bundle and, on first Dark use, parse the 2026 Dark JSON source
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional fixed source asset per page bundle and at most one parse per page for Dark use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The page bundled the existing built-in themes but not 2026-dark.json, and Dark Modern was parsed as the Dark root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bundle transfer/module initialization is part of explorer startup; JSONC parsing is part of first Dark render. Neither scales with fixture count after caching.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed size of the newly bundled 2026-dark.json asset. Rendering more fixtures does not retain additional copies or repeat loading for the same theme object.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Explorer UI may render fixtures in parallel, but Dark theme setup is coalesced through a shared promise. No queue, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, or network operation is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The module-level theme string remains for the page lifetime, as all existing bundled theme resources do. Theme parsing is lazy until Dark is requested and then cached; there is no negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the fixed eager bundle addition and single lazy parse; high that coalescing prevents repetition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The precise startup-byte and parse-time delta is not measured, but the source is bounded to one theme file and no realistic multiplicative trigger was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The bounded asset increase is intrinsic to making the theme available and does not establish meaningful latency, CPU, GC, or memory degradation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Viewing the committed blocks-ci screenshot baseline Markdown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A Markdown renderer may fetch each visible remote screenshot URL to display the document. The diff replaces hashes for Dark screenshots but does not add image entries or change the service endpoint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch content-addressed screenshot images when the Markdown document is rendered
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per rendered image entry both before and after; the diff changes Dark image keys without increasing entry count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Markdown entries fetched images from the same service using the prior hashes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Individual images require their fetch to display, but document structure and request fan-out are unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of screenshot entries visible/requested by the Markdown client. Effective cardinality is unchanged because each modified URL replaces one previous URL.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Image fetch concurrency is controlled by the Markdown/browser client and is unchanged by the diff; no application-side batching or queue changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Changed content-addressed URLs will be cold until fetched, while unchanged Light/high-contrast URLs retain their existing cache keys. This is the expected finite invalidation for changed images, with no unbounded key retention in repository code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that URL hashes alone changed and cardinality is preserved.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual client caching and lazy image loading vary, but there is no changed request cardinality or payload-size evidence in the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. New hashes necessarily invalidate caches for changed screenshots, but no new or scaling network mechanism is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff and traced fixture startup, first-use theme loading, repeated fixture renders, CI screenshot capture, and baseline Markdown viewing. The added theme work is fixed-size and coalesced; no high-confidence actionable performance regression or regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
